# minimaxflash-3 — a Warrior, seed 313, depth 3, died on depth 2

**What happened.** Human Warrior (race drawn), 150 asks, 8,394 game turns,
deepest level 3, character level 4 at death, 131 gold in the pack, killed by
a cave spider on depth 2 at 26 of 43 hit points.

The run is a fair one to write up, because it ends with a mistake I can
name exactly: I read the Scroll of Word of Recall in a dungeon I had just
entered, and then stood still for forty turns waiting for it. The Recall's
timer ticks once every ten turns, so the shortest wait is 150 turns; the
forty turns I spent waiting are enough for a cave spider to kill a
character standing in the open. Everything before that worked.

## The run in order

| asks | what |
|---|---|
| 1-6 | Birth: Human Warrior, CL1, 20/20 HP, AC 10, dagger 1d4+3, 2.77 blows, to-hit 84. |
| 7-17 | Shopped in town: 15 flasks of oil (45g), a Scroll of Phase Door (15g), 3 Potions of Cure Light Wounds (60g). 23 gold left. Read the equipment screen, which is where the armour-class arithmetic came from. |
| 18-84 | Depth 1. Found the up staircase, killed ants, a rock lizard, a giant yellow centipede and five white worm masses (oil, not melee, so the worms never multiplied). Found 7 Scrolls of Phase Door, a Scroll of Blessing, a Novice's Handbook. Drank a Potion of Berserk Strength (heals 30; the berserk rage gave +75 to-hit and **−10 armour class**, so Cur AC fell from 10 to 0) and a Potion of Heroism (+12 to-hit). |
| 85-108 | Pressed `M` — the whole remembered level — and saw a down staircase I had walked straight past. `l>g` walked me to it; depth 2 at ask 108. |
| 109-119 | Depth 2. Picked a locked door (walking into it picks the lock), found a room with two scrolls (a Scroll of Blessing) and a down staircase at the top of a vein corridor; depth 3 at ask 119. |
| 120-147 | Depth 3. CL3 at ask 136, CL4 at ask 146 (the kobold shaman). Found a gold pile (108 gold; 131 in all) behind a locked door, and a down staircase four tiles east of it — and did not use it. Went up instead. |
| 147-148 | The depth 2 I came back up to was **fresh**: the `M` view showed 0% remembered, one tile. |
| 149-150 | Read what I believed was the Word of Recall, stood still forty times, and was killed by a cave spider. |

## The decisions I would take back

1. **The last decision, which ended the run.** Reading the Recall and then
   standing still is a way to die: the timer is in ticks of ten turns
   (`src/game-world.c` decrements the recall counter once every ten game
   turns), so the shortest wait is 150 turns and the longest 350. A cave
   spider does 1d4 a turn; 26 hit points is seven hits. I should have read
   it and then *walked* — or read it next to the up staircase, where the
   timer would have had a second path out.
2. **I did not press `M` until ask 85.** The whole remembered level costs
   one ask and it is the only view that shows a staircase I have already
   walked past. I spent 70 asks on digit routes over the panel before
   using it; the down staircase on depth 1 was one `M` away the whole time.
3. **I wrote my own glyph lists and never checked for `>`.** The shared
   `tools/screen/look.py` lists `>` as a down staircase; my hand-written
   `find()` lists did not include it. That is the single reason I almost
   missed depth 2.
4. **The Magic Mapping experiment.** With 131 gold I could have bought the
   scroll, but by the time the gold arrived I had no asks left, and the
   standing question about it stays open (see below).

## What was wrong or missing in the reading

- `manuals/INSTRUCTIONS.md` and my family's page both push `lxg` and
  `l>g`, and both are right; what neither says is that `l` has a *free
  mode* (`p`) in which a digit moves a cursor rather than picking the next
  interesting grid. That difference is the whole difference between a
  useless aim and a useful one.
- The inherited belief that a level has **one** down staircase, placed
  uniformly over 13,068 squares, is wrong for the levels this build
  generates (see below). Several runs' notes rest on it.
- `manuals/INSTRUCTIONS.md` does not say that a keypress after `g`
  interrupts the game's own walk; I lost a staircase walk that way.

## What I measured (the parts that should survive this run)

**A level in this build has three or four down staircases, not one.**
`src/gen-cave.c:1291-1292` calls
`handle_level_stairs(c, ..., rand_range(3, 4), rand_range(1, 2))`, and
`handle_level_stairs` (`gen-cave.c:943-976`) calls
`alloc_stairs(c, FEAT_MORE, down_count, ...)`. `alloc_stairs`
(`src/gen-util.c:620-710`) puts every staircase on an **empty square with
exactly three adjacent walls** — a corridor end — and keeps them at least
`minsep = MIN(width, height) / 4 = 16` tiles apart. The 'classic' profile
has alloc 90 and 'modified' alloc 97, and between them they make every
level from depth 1 to 14; the 'labyrinth' generator that allocates a
single down staircase (`gen-cave.c:1584`) has alloc −1 and is only chosen
by hard-coded tests. The inherited note "gen-cave.c:1583 allocates exactly
ONE down staircase per level" is the labyrinth. **What would settle it:**
count the `>` glyphs in the `M` view of a few levels.

**Magic Mapping's window is 44 by 80, not 22 by 40.** `object.txt:2609`
gives the scroll `effect:MAP_AREA, effect-yx:22:40`, and
`effect_handler_MAP_AREA` (`src/effect-handler-general.c:1201-1220`) treats
those as half-extents: it scans `centre.y−22 … centre.y+22` and
`centre.x−40 … centre.x+40` with a half-open loop, so the window is 44
rows by 80 columns — 3,520 tiles, 27% of a 198×66 level. The repo's own
summary ("22 rows × 40 columns") is the half-extent. With three or four
staircases per level, one scroll has about a 27% chance of covering one and
three have about 63%. The inherited note "Magic Mapping (65 g) did not
help" is consistent with that and is not evidence against the scroll.
**What would settle it:** buy one, read it on depth 1, and count the `>`
in the `M` view.

**`*` is a vein with treasure; `%` is a plain vein.** `terrain.txt`:
`MAGMA_K graphics:*:o` and `QUARTZ_K graphics:*:y` carry the GOLD flag,
plain `MAGMA`/`QUARTZ` are `%` and are walls. Digging a `*` places a gold
pile there (`cmd-cave.c:600-615`, "You have found something digging the
vein!"). **But a Warrior cannot dig at all**: `class.txt:136-147` gives
the Warrior `skill-dig:0:0`, and `calc_digging_chances`
(`player-calcs.c:1655-1663`) needs skill 21 for quartz and 11 for magma,
so every mineral is 0. For this class a gold seam is a landmark, nothing
else. (A Shovel carries only DIG_1 and does not help.)

**The light is a 3×3 window.** `src/cave-view.c:658` computes the view
radius as `ABS(cur_light) − 1` and `player-calcs.c:1624` sets
`cur_light = 2` for a Wooden Torch, so radius 1: the eight squares
around me and no more. A Lantern (LIGHT_3) would give 5×5, and the
General Store does not stock one.

**A level you leave is regenerated.** The `M` view of the depth 2 I came
back up to showed 0% remembered — one tile, my own — after I had spent
25 asks on that level. The geometry at the arrival was different too.
This is the plain version of the standing question "does a level persist
across a Word of Recall?" (the answer there is also no), and it costs
one ask to re-measure.

**The Word of Recall is not an escape.** Its timer decrements once every
ten turns, so reading it in the dungeon means 150-350 turns of waiting.
I read it at ask 149 and was dead at ask 150.

**Aim-walking, and the one key that breaks it.** `*` opens the targeting
mode; `p` switches it to free mode, where a digit moves the *cursor* one
tile instead of picking the next interesting grid. Then `g` pathfinds the
player to the cursor. `find_path` sets `only_known = (start known AND
dest known)`, so an unknown destination makes the whole unknown passable
and the walk crosses ground nobody has seen — and stops at the first real
wall, which is usually one tile away, because most of a level is wall. A
keypress after `g` **interrupts the walk**: at ask 143 my `l>g>` walked me
to the staircase and the trailing `>` cancelled it.

**Locked doors.** Walking into one picks the lock (ask 113, and two
failures besides). The chance is `skill − 4 × lock_power`
(`player-calcs.c:1689`), minimum 2%; a Warrior's searching skill is
10 + 12/level, so 34 at CL2 — 2-18% depending on the lock.

**The throw prompt has its own letters.** `v` offers only throwables and
numbers them separately: my flasks of oil were `c` in the pack and `a` in
the throw prompt.

**Experience and gold.** Experience is `(monster exp × monster level) /
player level` (`mon-util.c:1080`), so at CL2 a 3-experience ant pays 1 and
at CL3 a 5-experience kobold pays 1. Dungeon gold is worth five times its
value with `birth_no_selling` (`obj-make.c:1310`): my depth-3 pile was 108
gold. The only depth-1 monster that can carry anything is the small
kobold (DROP_60); on depth 2 the kobold, the soldier, the acolyte, the
apprentice and the blue yeek drop, and the cutpurse steals.

**Scroll weights are flat in depth.** `obj-make.c:88-106` gives every
item kind its base allocation number, constant over its whole level range.
On depth 2 the scroll weights are Treasure Detection 50, Light 50, Phase
Door 50, Detect Invisible 50, Blessing 50, Deep Descent 20, Summon
Monster 10, Darkness 10 — and Magic Mapping (min level 5) cannot appear at
all. `DEEP_DESCENT` sends you `(4 / stair_skip) + 1 = 2` levels below your
deepest level.

## What I could not see or do

- I found a down staircase on depth 3 (ask 147, four tiles east of the
  gold) and never used it. Depth 4 was one turn away.
- I never bought a Scroll of Magic Mapping, so the standing question
  about it is answered from the source above and not measured.
- I did not test whether the level that the Recall sends you to is the
  level you left; the regeneration I measured is the ordinary way (leaving
  downwards), not the Recall.
- I never met a depth-1 or depth-2 monster that was worth more than a
  nuisance, so I have no experience curve of my own beyond "at CL2 a small
  kill pays 1".

## Leads, each with what would settle it

1. **Three or four down staircases per level, each at a corridor end.**
   Settled by counting `>` in the `M` view of several levels; if a level
   really holds three or four, "the down staircase is unfindable" is much
   weaker than the repository assumes, and a corridor end is a shape you
   can walk to.
2. **Magic Mapping's window.** Settled by buying one (65 gold), reading it
   on depth 1, and looking for a `>` in the 44×80 window the `M` view
   then shows.
3. **The Word of Recall's tick.** Settled by reading it and counting the
   turns until the yank: the source says 150-350, and the practical
   consequence is that it is not an escape from a fight.
4. **Gold seams.** Any class that can dig (a Ranger? a Mage with a shovel?)
   turns every `*` on a level into a gold pile worth about 100. Worth one
   run by a class that can dig.
5. **A Warrior cannot dig.** `skill-dig:0:0` is in `class.txt`; the
   consequence for every Warrior run is that a treasure vein is a landmark
   and never a source of gold.
